medical.title: New wrist stimulation device brings relief for people with Tourette's
medical.summary: People living with Tourette's can now benefit from a new device developed using research from the University of Nottingham. Spinoff company Neurotherapeutics Ltd. has launched the Neupulse C wellness wrist device. The device provides gentle, noninvasive stimulation to support calm and relaxation during moments of restlessness or physical tension.

medical.title: Chronic intestinal inflammation can affect heart through changes in gut microbiota and immune cells, study finds
medical.summary: Chronic intestinal inflammation drives cardiac dysfunction through a gut microbiota-dependent pathway, suggesting a potential therapeutic target for reducing cardiovascular risk in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), according to a study led by researchers in the Institute for Biomedical Sciences at Georgia State University.

medical.title: Expert joins international call for new approach to diagnosing, managing condition known as POTS
medical.summary: For people living with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, or POTS, the simple act of standing up can cause a cascade of symptoms: a racing heart, lightheadedness, brain fog, shakiness and exhaustion. Yet a standard cardiac test may appear completely normal.

medical.title: ‘I can breathe again’. Readers share their experiences of a more balanced media diet
medical.summary: We often talk about the impact journalism has on democracy and how we understand the world. But what about its impact on how we feel? The post ‘I can breathe again’. Readers share their experiences of a more balanced media diet appeared first on Positive News .

medical.title: Which is more filling, protein or fiber?
medical.summary: Protein has been everywhere lately. You may have seen food products promoting high protein content or reels online telling you how to boost your intake. One of the ways protein supports our health is by helping a meal fill us up (satiation) and keeping us feeling fuller for longer between meals (satiety). It does this by influencing our appetite hormones and other metabolic processes.

medical.title: Are we trying too hard to sleep? How 'sleepmaxxing' could be keeping us awake
medical.summary: Too hot, too cold. On your stomach, then your side. Thoughts spiraling. Counting sheep. Checking the clock. Unable to sleep.

medical.title: Program helping patients self-regulate strong-opioid use has potential for NHS, study shows
medical.summary: A new support program can increase the number of patients who successfully self-regulate their long-term intake of strong opioid painkillers without worsening their quality of life, a study has shown.

medical.title: Nearly 1 in 3 new nurse practitioners educated at for-profit schools, study finds
medical.summary: For-profit schools appear to be playing an outsized role in training the nation's expanding nurse practitioner workforce, according to a study that found nearly one-third of newly licensed nurse practitioners in four states were educated at for-profit programs in 2024, up from just 2.4% in 2010.

medical.title: Does a bone tumor always mean cancer?
medical.summary: Bone tumors can cause symptoms such as persistent pain and unintended weight loss, or they might only be discovered when someone breaks a bone and X-rays show a lesion. Wendy Allen-Rhoades, M.D., Ph.D., a pediatric oncologist at Mayo Clinic Comprehensive Cancer Center, describes the most common bone cancers in children and adults.

medical.title: Pain, psychological factors and physical function closely linked in people with systemic sclerosis
medical.summary: For many people living with chronic conditions like systemic sclerosis, pain can be persistent, unpredictable and difficult to manage. This can affect mood, worry, sleep, motivation and confidence in completing daily activities.

medical.title: Only one workout helped older adults lose fat and keep muscle
medical.summary: A six-month study suggests that high-intensity interval training (HIIT) may offer older adults a powerful advantage: losing body fat while keeping their muscle. Unlike moderate-intensity workouts, which led to a small loss of lean muscle, HIIT preserved it while also improving body composition around the waist.

medical.title: Age and sex shape cancer immunity, mouse experiments and human data suggest
medical.summary: A new study published in Nature Aging combines mouse experiments and human data sets to explore how biological sex and aging shape cancer immunity, with implications for immunotherapy responses. Lutz Menzel, Ph.D., formerly of the Department of Radiation Oncology within the Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute, is the lead author, and Tim Padera, Ph.D., of the Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute, is the senior author. The paper is titled "Lymph node contraction links sex-biased naive CD8 T cell decline to compromised antigen recognition during middle age."

medical.title: Three surprising reasons to slow down for a thoughtful, nutritious breakfast
medical.summary: From cognitive function to reinforcing family bonds, the benefits of making time for good, whole foods in the morning are plentiful The post Three surprising reasons to slow down for a thoughtful, nutritious breakfast appeared first on Positive News .

medical.title: Nearly 30,000 people tested quit-smoking methods. One stood out
medical.summary: Nicotine e-cigarettes appear to help more smokers quit than patches, gum, and several other common approaches, according to a major review of 80 clinical trials. Researchers say regulated vaping products are not risk-free, but may be a significantly less harmful alternative for people who would otherwise continue smoking.

medical.title: Scientists tested 5 natural compounds on cancer cells. One stood out
medical.summary: Five natural compounds, including curcumin and berberine, were tested for their effects on cancer cells and healthy muscle cells. All disrupted cancer cell energy production and pushed many of the cells into a non-dividing state, with curcumin producing the strongest overall effect. Curcumin also showed a relatively favorable safety profile, while some other compounds caused more toxicity.

science.title: Physics model reveals fundamental trade-off between prediction and energy efficiency in intelligent systems
science.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly becoming part of our everyday lives, from digital assistants to robots that respond to their surroundings. Each of these capabilities is based on physical computational processes that consume energy. An international research team led by Hans Briegel from the Department of Theoretical Physics at the University of Innsbruck, Austria, has investigated the physical limits on the efficiency with which intelligent systems process information. Their findings are published in Physical Review X.

science.title: My son goes to the gym a lot. How can I tell if this is healthy or a sign something is wrong?
science.summary: A teenage boy goes to the gym several times a week. He takes protein powder and watches what he eats carefully. He talks about being "ripped" or "jacked."

science.title: Offering alcohol-free beer on tap boosts pub choices while keeping revenues intact, new study shows
science.summary: Simple changes to pub environments can encourage drinkers to choose alcohol-free options without harming profits, according to new research from the University of York. The study, published in Drug and Alcohol Review, evaluated how introducing alcohol-free (AF) beer through three sequential behavioral "nudges" influenced consumer habits and revenues across three distinct U.K. pubs.

science.title: New research reveals surprising link in ocean carbon cycle: Swimming sea cucumbers
science.summary: New MBARI research has revealed that the sea cucumber Pelagothuria natatrix plays an important and unexpected role in the ocean's carbon cycle. In a new article published in the journal Ecology, senior scientist Bruce Robison reports that this unique swimming sea cucumber is a prominent member of the midwater community in the Galápagos Islands, intercepting carbon sinking to the deep seafloor.

science.title: Superconducting circuit links smaller photon groups into larger entangled states
science.summary: Quantum computers, computer systems that leverage the laws of quantum mechanics, store and process information using qubits (i.e., quantum bits). In many quantum computers, qubits are linked via entanglement, a quantum mechanical effect that connects particles in such a way that their shared state cannot be described as separate, independent states.

science.title: Is this the 'mathocalypse'? Why OpenAI's latest results dump has left mathematicians in shock
science.summary: Earlier this week, OpenAI published a trove of hundreds of mathematical results it claimed could "push the frontier of human knowledge." Produced largely by an unreleased artificial intelligence (AI) model, the 722 papers relate to 372 open problems covering everything from algebra and geometry to theoretical computer science.

science.title: YouTube overtakes TV as top source of political news, study finds
science.summary: The Center for the Creator Economy at Syracuse University—the nation's first academic center dedicated to the advancement of interdisciplinary academics, independent research, policy engagement and support for creator-based ventures—today released the findings from its inaugural industry Flash Report. Published monthly, these reports examine the issues creators, brands and audiences are talking about right now.

science.title: How much noise should we put up with? London and Copenhagen have different answers
science.summary: Traffic, trains, nightlife—in cities everywhere, there is a near-constant background hum that most people simply get used to.

science.title: Are autistic suspects likely to be disadvantaged in forensic interviews?
science.summary: A new study led by Flinders University finds both autistic and nonautistic suspects may be judged more harshly if any idiosyncratic behaviors in interviews stray beyond what observers consider normal. The research also undermines the widely held perspective—referred to as the "double empathy hypothesis"—that autistic people can better "read" differing intentions and motivations in other autistic people than nonautistic people can.

science.title: Scientists find hidden materials that could improve batteries and solar fuels
science.summary: Scientists have uncovered a hidden world of “in-between” materials that briefly form as chemical ingredients are heated, revealing structures that conventional methods can miss. Among the discoveries is a previously unknown form of bismuth vanadate, a material widely studied for using sunlight to help produce clean hydrogen. The new version has a different atomic structure and interacts with light in a strikingly different way, potentially opening new possibilities for solar fuels, catalysts, and electronics.

science.title: Walking through flames: Orangutans rescued in Indonesia fires
science.summary: The orangutan clings to the top of a mostly leafless tree in Indonesia's portion of Borneo as waves of thick smoke from the forest fires burning below waft over her.

science.title: Seals and sea lions get their hearing tested at Australia Zoo
science.summary: Scientists in Australia trained sea lions and seals to respond to a hearing test for research into how the marine mammals are affected by human-made noise.

science.title: Malaysia closes schools in capital, parts of country due to haze
science.summary: Malaysia closed schools in Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country Friday as haze from fires in neighboring Indonesia again pushed local air quality to some of the world's worst levels.

science.title: Fish may look fine in urban waters but their genes tell a different story
science.summary: Blue damselfish, with their striking blue hue, are easy to spot, even along Okinawa's heavily urbanized coastlines. But while abundant, their gene activity reveals a hidden cost to living in human-impacted environments.

science.title: 'Molecular movie' finally reveals how penicillin is made
science.summary: Researchers from the University of Oxford and international collaborators have revealed previously unseen rapid chemical stages in the formation of β-lactam antibiotics like penicillin, offering insights that can support future antibiotic development. The findings have been published in Nature Catalysis.

science.title: 3D genome 'entanglement' may explain how cephalopods evolved complex brains
science.summary: Octopuses, squid and cuttlefish, collectively known as coleoid cephalopods, have evolved exceptionally large and elaborately structured nervous systems capable of complex behaviors such as problem-solving and rapid camouflage. A new study by scientists at the University of Vienna suggests that the origins of this complexity may lie not just in the genes themselves, but in how the genome is organized in 3D.

science.title: A 9-billion-year-old signal could help explain dark energy
science.summary: A Canadian radio telescope has detected the faint glow of hydrogen from billions of years ago using only its own observations, proving a long-awaited way to map the distant universe can actually work. CHIME can use this hydrogen signal to trace how matter is spread across space and measure how the universe has expanded over time, offering a powerful new way to investigate dark energy.

science.title: A quantum prediction from 1931 just came to life
science.summary: Nearly a century after physicist Hans Bethe predicted them, scientists have created and directly observed unusual quantum states known as “Bethe strings” in an ultracold gas. By cooling cesium atoms to near absolute zero and trapping them in thousands of tiny one-dimensional tubes, researchers were able to make groups of atoms bind together without ordinary chemical bonds. These strange clusters could contain six or more particles and even collide with one another without falling apart.

science.title: Four astronauts return to Earth after eight months in space
science.summary: Four astronauts returned to Earth from the International Space Station on Thursday after hurrying there eight months ago to replace an ailing colleague and his crew.

science.title: NASA astronauts splash down after 100 million miles in space
science.summary: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 astronauts have returned to Earth after 237 days in space, traveling more than 100 million miles and completing over 3,792 orbits while conducting research to prepare for future missions to the Moon and Mars. mix_items.summary: Malaysia closed schools in Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country Friday as haze from fires in neighboring Indonesia again pushed local air quality to some of the world's worst levels.

mix_items.title: Fish may look fine in urban waters but their genes tell a different story
mix_items.summary: Blue damselfish, with their striking blue hue, are easy to spot, even along Okinawa's heavily urbanized coastlines. But while abundant, their gene activity reveals a hidden cost to living in human-impacted environments.

mix_items.title: 'Molecular movie' finally reveals how penicillin is made
mix_items.summary: Researchers from the University of Oxford and international collaborators have revealed previously unseen rapid chemical stages in the formation of β-lactam antibiotics like penicillin, offering insights that can support future antibiotic development. The findings have been published in Nature Catalysis.

mix_items.title: 3D genome 'entanglement' may explain how cephalopods evolved complex brains
mix_items.summary: Octopuses, squid and cuttlefish, collectively known as coleoid cephalopods, have evolved exceptionally large and elaborately structured nervous systems capable of complex behaviors such as problem-solving and rapid camouflage. A new study by scientists at the University of Vienna suggests that the origins of this complexity may lie not just in the genes themselves, but in how the genome is organized in 3D.

mix_items.title: Age and sex shape cancer immunity, mouse experiments and human data suggest
mix_items.summary: A new study published in Nature Aging combines mouse experiments and human data sets to explore how biological sex and aging shape cancer immunity, with implications for immunotherapy responses. Lutz Menzel, Ph.D., formerly of the Department of Radiation Oncology within the Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute, is the lead author, and Tim Padera, Ph.D., of the Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute, is the senior author. The paper is titled "Lymph node contraction links sex-biased naive CD8 T cell decline to compromised antigen recognition during middle age."

mix_items.title: A 9-billion-year-old signal could help explain dark energy
mix_items.summary: A Canadian radio telescope has detected the faint glow of hydrogen from billions of years ago using only its own observations, proving a long-awaited way to map the distant universe can actually work. CHIME can use this hydrogen signal to trace how matter is spread across space and measure how the universe has expanded over time, offering a powerful new way to investigate dark energy.

mix_items.title: A quantum prediction from 1931 just came to life
mix_items.summary: Nearly a century after physicist Hans Bethe predicted them, scientists have created and directly observed unusual quantum states known as “Bethe strings” in an ultracold gas. By cooling cesium atoms to near absolute zero and trapping them in thousands of tiny one-dimensional tubes, researchers were able to make groups of atoms bind together without ordinary chemical bonds. These strange clusters could contain six or more particles and even collide with one another without falling apart.

mix_items.title: Four astronauts return to Earth after eight months in space
mix_items.summary: Four astronauts returned to Earth from the International Space Station on Thursday after hurrying there eight months ago to replace an ailing colleague and his crew.

mix_items.title: Three surprising reasons to slow down for a thoughtful, nutritious breakfast
mix_items.summary: From cognitive function to reinforcing family bonds, the benefits of making time for good, whole foods in the morning are plentiful The post Three surprising reasons to slow down for a thoughtful, nutritious breakfast appeared first on Positive News .

mix_items.title: NASA astronauts splash down after 100 million miles in space
mix_items.summary: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 astronauts have returned to Earth after 237 days in space, traveling more than 100 million miles and completing over 3,792 orbits while conducting research to prepare for future missions to the Moon and Mars. The mission also made history with record-setting spacewalk achievements and experiments that could transform medicine both in space and on Earth.

mix_items.title: Nearly 30,000 people tested quit-smoking methods. One stood out
mix_items.summary: Nicotine e-cigarettes appear to help more smokers quit than patches, gum, and several other common approaches, according to a major review of 80 clinical trials. Researchers say regulated vaping products are not risk-free, but may be a significantly less harmful alternative for people who would otherwise continue smoking.

mix_items.title: Scientists tested 5 natural compounds on cancer cells. One stood out
mix_items.summary: Five natural compounds, including curcumin and berberine, were tested for their effects on cancer cells and healthy muscle cells. All disrupted cancer cell energy production and pushed many of the cells into a non-dividing state, with curcumin producing the strongest overall effect. Curcumin also showed a relatively favorable safety profile, while some other compounds caused more toxicity.

mix_items.title: Activists cite ecological, social connections in blocking US border wall construction (commentary)
mix_items.summary: A group of activists in the small border town of Lochiel, Arizona, U.S., is fighting to save 200-year-old cottonwood trees by stopping contractors from building a section of the U.S.’s new wall along its border with Mexico. One activist lived for over 70 days in the upper branches of an ancient cottonwood dubbed the “Grandmother […]

mix_items.title: Crackdown reveals ‘industrial-scale’ wildlife and timber trafficking across Latin America
mix_items.summary: Authorities across nine Latin American and Caribbean countries have arrested hundreds of people and recovered more than 1,000 animals as part of a two-month coordinated operation against environmental crimes. Operation Madre Tierra was the eighth edition of a recurring Interpol-led initiative, and was conducted in June and July in Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, […]

mix_items.title: South Korea strengthens migrant fisher protections. Advocates are not impressed.
mix_items.summary: SEOUL — At 2 a.m. one night, two Indonesian fishers were gripping a flimsy, makeshift rope, hanging on for dear life. The precarious rope dangled from the eighth-floor window of a motel room overlooking a dark alley in the South Korean port city of Busan, swinging left and right with the wind. The men had […]

mix_items.title: Australia’s new eco police flexes muscles with major wildlife trafficking bust
mix_items.summary: Australian authorities have disrupted an alleged wildlife trafficking syndicate, uncovering a clandestine operation where smuggled native animals were hoarded alongside caches of cash and gold, reports contributor Johan Augustin for Mongabay. The operation reportedly seized 28 native and a few exotic species alongside approximately A$300,000 (nearly $210,000) in cash, gold, and silver bullion on July […]

mix_items.title: Invasive species have more severe environmental impacts in Global South, study finds
mix_items.summary: The environmental impacts caused by invasive alien species are more severe in poor countries of Global South than wealthy countries of Global North, a new study finds. The study shatters a long-standing assumption that wealthier Global North countries suffer the worst effects of invasive alien species (IAS) and highlights weak governance and insufficient management capacity […]

mix_items.title: Did two of the lemurs stolen in Bangladesh end up in India? Officials are investigating
mix_items.summary: The case of three ring-tailed lemurs, an endangered species, stolen from Gazipur Safari Park in Bangladesh last year resurfaced on social media in September this year, when news spread that two of the lemurs were trafficked to India and later sheltered at a private wildlife conservation facility, Vantara. The viral news prompted Vantara to release […]

mix_items.title: Logging threatens Bornean forest earmarked for Indigenous Peace Park
mix_items.summary: Part of a forest in Malaysian Borneo that Indigenous communities had envisioned co-managing and self-governing has been turned into an active commercial logging concession, according to a recent civil society report. The 283,500-hectare (700,500-acre) Upper Baram Forest Area, in the northeastern part of the state of Sarawak, was proposed as a community-led conservation area more […]

mix_items.title: Scientists were wrong about this strange mammal for nearly 40 years
mix_items.summary: A beautifully preserved fossil from Mongolia’s Gobi Desert has solved a mystery that puzzled paleontologists for nearly 40 years. Tamirkhan balcarceli shows that zhelestids were not early relatives of modern placental mammals, despite having teeth that seemed to suggest they were. Instead, the rabbit-like animal belonged to a separate lineage of small Cretaceous mammals.
